verdict.rationale: Lithic provides infrastructure for autonomous background decisioning — Authorization Stream Access (real-time HTTP-based approval decisions), the Auth Rules v2 engine (program/account/card-level rules, shadow mode, backtesting) and Events/webhooks for automated event delivery — and explicitly markets 'autonomous issuing, payments, and controls for AI-powered workflows' for agentic commerce. However, this is developer-built automation via API/webhooks rather than a turnkey 'set up an automation and it runs' experience within an AI assistant; the MCP integration is presented as an in-editor coding aid, not itself the mechanism for persistent background automation. Missing for 10: evidence of a no-code/AI-assistant-driven automation builder, scheduling/triggers UI, or hands-on proof that autonomous rules run unattended without developer-managed infrastructure.
